title: Alerting contract
description: The promise made before anything pages, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #69: a severity ladder with dated rungs, runbooks with escalation clocks, and alert rules that name an owner, a severity from the ladder, a runbook, and a record destination. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/alerts); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — rung names unique, rung definedOn dates real and not in the future, alert severities on the ladder and not defined after the contract's own review, runbook ids unique and resolvable from every alert rule, and one warning a schema cannot express: a runbook no alert rule points at.

version.description: Version of the contract. The ladder and runbooks are versioned like code — an alert set that can silently change is folklore, not a contract.

reviewedOn.description: Date the contract was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future.

severityLadder.description: The severity ladder, ordered as written. Each rung carries the day it was defined, so the gate can prove a severity existed before the incident that used it.

name.description: Severity name, e.g. sev-1. Unique across the ladder; alerts and incidents cite it verbatim.

description.description: What this severity means, in terms you are willing to say out loud. A severity nobody can define is a severity nobody can assign.

definedOn.description: The day this rung was defined, YYYY-MM-DD. The gate fails an incident graded with a severity defined after the incident was detected.

runbooks.description: The runbooks the alert rules point at. Each carries its escalation clock — who escalates, by when.

id.description: Runbook id. Unique across the contract; alert rules reference it.

link.description: Where the runbook lives. The runbook must be a place you can go.

escalationClock.description: Who escalates, by when — e.g. 'Acknowledge in 15 minutes; escalate to the on-call lead at 60'. A runbook without its clock is a wiki page, not a runbook.

alerts.description: The alert rules. Each names an owner, a severity from the ladder, a runbook, and a record destination — all four, or the rule does not ship.

id.description: Alert rule id. Unique across the contract; the incident register cites it when the alert fires.

owner.description: Who owns the alert and answers for it. A page nobody owns is nobody's page.

severity.description: A name from severityLadder. The validator fails a severity that is not on the ladder, or that was defined on the ladder after the contract's own review date.

runbook.description: The runbook id this rule points at. Must be declared in this contract.

recordDestination.description: Where the record goes when this alert fires. Nothing pages without creating a record — say where.
